questions.question: Differentiate between wired and wireless eavesdropping. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between wired and wireless eavesdropping. [U/CO3]
  • Core: Wired requires access to switch/tap/SPAN; wireless can be captured over-the-
  • air; wireless adds RF range/SSID/MAC issues; encryption differences (WEP/WPA).
  • Marking:
  • Full 2: States medium difference and access modality (cable/switch vs RF),
  • mentions implication (range/encryption)
  • Partial 1 mark: Mentions only “wireless is over air” without contrast
  • CEH Sybex: Ch.6 pp.154–166; Ch.10 overview for wireless.

questions.question: Differentiate DNS, IP, and HTTPS sniffing in detail and illustrate their attack scenarios. / [CO3] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate DNS, IP, and HTTPS sniffing; illustrate attack scenarios. [U/CO3]
  • DNS sniffing: capture queries/responses; risks (hostnames, subdomains),
  • spoofing/poisoning angle.
  • IP sniffing: passive capture at L3/L2; unencrypted protocols; ARP poisoning to get
  • in-path; session hijack risk.
  • HTTPS sniffing: normally protected; scenarios where visible (misconfig, SSL
  • stripping, rogue CA, compromised proxy); HSTS role.
  • Tools: Wireshark, tcpdump, mitmproxy, Ettercap.
  • Mitigations: encryption, DNSSEC/DoT/DoH, ARP inspection, switch port security,
  • HSTS, certificate pinning.
  • For 13–15: clear distinctions, one scenario each, tool + countermeasure per type.
  • CEH Sybex: Ch.6 pp.158–166 (sniffing, ARP, DNS), Ch.7 hijacking.
